title: Wheatfield with Crows
author: Vincent van Gogh
about: Often called his last painting, though it wasn't: it is one of his final works, made in Auvers-sur-Oise in July 1890. Three paths that go nowhere under a storm sky.

title: Starry Night Over the Rhône
author: Vincent van Gogh
about: The river at Arles under the new gas lamps, painted outdoors at night a year before The Starry Night. The Big Dipper shines over the town.

title: Wheat Field with Cypresses
author: Vincent van Gogh
about: One of three versions made at Saint-Rémy. Van Gogh wrote that cypresses were as beautiful in line and proportion as an Egyptian obelisk.

title: Impression, Sunrise
author: Claude Monet
about: The port of Le Havre at dawn. A critic mocked its title in 1874, and the name of a whole movement, Impressionism, came from it.

title: Poppy Field near Argenteuil
author: Claude Monet
about: The mother and child in front are usually taken to be Monet's wife Camille and son Jean. It hung at the first Impressionist exhibition in 1874.

title: The Monk by the Sea
author: Caspar David Friedrich
about: One tiny figure before an empty sea and sky. With no foreground or path into the picture, it baffled Berlin when it was first shown.

title: Moonrise over the Sea
author: Caspar David Friedrich
about: Three figures on a rock watch sailing ships come home under the rising moon, a favourite Friedrich theme of waiting and longing.

title: The Oxbow
author: Thomas Cole
about: The Connecticut River after a thunderstorm: wild forest on the left, farmland on the right. Cole, founder of the Hudson River School, paints himself in at the bottom.

title: Among the Sierra Nevada, California
author: Albert Bierstadt
about: Painted in Rome and shown across Europe. Not a real view: an idealised composite of the American West, built to astonish.

title: Twilight in the Wilderness
author: Frederic Edwin Church
about: A blazing sunset over the Maine wilderness, painted months before the American Civil War; many have read the burning sky as an omen.

title: The Heart of the Andes
author: Frederic Edwin Church
about: Built from Church's travels in Ecuador. In 1859 New Yorkers paid to see it in a darkened room, some studying the detail through opera glasses.

title: The Fighting Temeraire
author: J. M. W. Turner
about: A warship that fought at Trafalgar is towed by a steam tug to be broken up: the sun setting on the age of sail. Voted Britain's greatest painting in 2005.

title: The Hay Wain
author: John Constable
about: A farm cart in the River Stour by Flatford Mill, Suffolk. Ignored at home at first, it won a gold medal at the Paris Salon of 1824.

title: The Ninth Wave
author: Ivan Aivazovsky
about: Survivors cling to a mast as the sun rises after a night storm. Sailors' lore says the ninth wave is the biggest. Aivazovsky painted his seas from memory.

title: Morning in a Pine Forest
author: Ivan Shishkin and Konstantin Savitsky
about: Shishkin painted the forest, Savitsky the bears; the collector Tretyakov removed Savitsky's signature. In Russia it is famous from a sweet wrapper.

title: Moonlit Night on the Dnieper
author: Arkhip Kuindzhi
about: Shown alone in a dark room with light only on the canvas. The moonlight glowed so much that visitors looked behind it for a lamp.

title: Above Eternal Peace
author: Isaac Levitan
about: A small wooden church on a bluff over Lake Udomlya. Levitan wrote that all of himself was in this picture.

title: Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Red Fuji)
author: Katsushika Hokusai
about: From Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. On late-summer mornings the early sun really can turn the mountain red.

title: A Storm in the Rocky Mountains, Mt. Rosalie
author: Albert Bierstadt
about: Bierstadt named the peak after Rosalie Ludlow, then married to his travelling companion. She later divorced him and married Bierstadt.

title: Niagara
author: Frederic Edwin Church
about: Painted with no shore in the foreground, so you seem to hang over the Horseshoe Falls. It made Church famous when shown in New York and London.

title: Water Lilies
author: Claude Monet
about: Part of the giant panels Monet painted of his pond at Giverny in his last years, while cataracts clouded his sight.

title: The Starry Night
author: Vincent van Gogh
about: Painted at the asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence from the view out of his window before sunrise. The cypress and the village were added from imagination.
